This document reports only on the completed E01/E02 blinded-review track.

interRaterAgreement.kappaInterpretation: Landis & Koch (1977) scale: kappa > 0.80 = almost perfect agreement. kappa = 1.0 here means perfect agreement -- observed on this controlled 15-sample set only; this is not asserted as a general property of these two raters or of expert review of FIGM's output beyond this sample.

figmVsConsensus.note: No sample was excluded because E01 and E02 disagreed on 0 of 15 samples. Consensus label equals both experts' shared label for every sample.

researchIntegrityStatements.notUniversalAccuracyClaim: FIGM achieved perfect agreement with both independent experts (E01 and E02) on this controlled 15-sample blinded-review set. This is not a claim of universal or population-level accuracy.
researchIntegrityStatements.notPopulationLevelValidation: This is a controlled, purposively small (n=15) sample drawn from FIGM's own testbed fixtures, evaluated by two independent human experts. It is not population-level validation and must not be cited as such.
researchIntegrityStatements.generalizationLimitation: These results are limited to the small controlled expert-review sample and should not be generalized as evidence of accuracy across all real-world SPA codebases.
researchIntegrityStatements.interRaterReliabilityHonesty: Cohen's kappa of 1.0 reflects perfect observed agreement between E01 and E02 on this specific 15-sample set. It is reported exactly as measured; no stronger or weaker inter-rater reliability claim is made than what this computation produced.
researchIntegrityStatements.pipelineSeparationStatement: This E01/E02 two-expert comparison is a completed, separate evidence track from the unrelated research/independent-annotation/ pipeline, which remains PENDING (0 submissions). The two must never be conflated or presented as the same evidence.
